introduction.text: The Mitreo dei Serpenti (V,VI,6) is a Roman Mithraic sanctuary located in the V region of Ostia. It is significant for its preserved architectural features and serpent-themed frescoes, which provide insight into the spread of Mithraism in the late Roman Empire.

history.description: The western walls of the sanctuary are built from tuff in a reticulated style dating to the 1st century BC.
The eastern walls of the sanctuary were constructed in two phases during the 2nd and 3rd centuries AD.
A fresco depicting a female serpent on the east wall and a male serpent with crest on the north wall predates the sanctuary, dating to the third quarter of the 3rd century AD.
The sanctuary was built in the second half of the 3rd century AD.

design.description: The sanctuary occupies a rectangular space of about 60 m², accessed from the northern short side.
The walls are constructed from tuff with a reticulated masonry technique.

art.description: A fresco of a female serpent on the east wall.
A fresco of a male serpent with crest on the north wall.
Remnants of a small altar at the base of the sanctuary.
